question: Alex has 5 pieces of paper, each with a different math problem. In how many ways can he give these problems to his 10 friends (he can give each friend more than one problem)?
solution:
For each of the five distinct problems, choose one of the ten friends as its recipient. A friend can receive multiple problems, so all ten choices remain available at every step. Each distribution corresponds to exactly one such list of recipients in problem order. By the multiplication principle there are 10⁵ = 100,000 distributions.
Final answer: 100,\!000
